Slow-motion gold liquid splashing around the bottle
A woman drawn to a man after one spray

insights.statement: In the Gulf, the scent you leave a guest with is the last word of your hospitality.
insights.tension: Hospitality is judged at the end of the visit, not the start.
insights.evidence: The host passes the bakhoor and the perfume to guests before they leave.
insights.gulf_meaning: Perfuming a parting guest is a ritual of generosity and respect in the majlis.

insights.statement: A scent is worn like a time of day: some people carry the golden hour with them.
insights.tension: People want to keep a feeling that passes in minutes.
insights.evidence: Everyone stops to watch the late sun through the mashrabiya.
insights.gulf_meaning: The light after asr has a warmth Gulf homes are built around.

insights.statement: The last thing you put on before the biggest night is the one you remember.
insights.tension: The groom is surrounded by people, but the last gesture is intimate.
insights.evidence: Friends fixing the bisht in the corridor before the zaffa.
insights.gulf_meaning: Gulf weddings are prepared by brothers and friends, hand by hand.
